findings.reason: the proof must take the optional-distribution set from a census run in the full shared environment (or from the declared extras), not from `build_census()` re-run inside the very environment it is proving; as written the proof's pass condition is unreachable for every optional subsystem import.
findings.text: the plan says the proof "imports `OPTIONAL_SUBSYSTEM_ROOTS` and `build_census()` ... so the proof and the census share one definition of optional", but `build_census()` (`tests/test_declared_dependencies.py:288`) classifies from the running interpreter's installed distributions: `module_distribution_map` (`:187`) builds its map from `packages_distributions()` and `distributions()`, and any imported module absent from that map lands in `unmapped` (`:316-319`) rather than in a `Row`; so in the fresh environment a plain sync has omitted (the plan's own §1 measured 61 extra-declared packages dropped), every optional distribution is uninstalled and therefore never classed "optional" — the proof cannot accept a `ModuleNotFoundError` "naming a distribution the census classed optional", which is its stated acceptance rule

findings.reason: the writer should route the fresh environment through the existing scratch resolver (or `$TMPDIR`) so the path follows the node's scratch rather than a hardcoded location that the owner already exists to abstract.
findings.text: §4 fixes node-local scratch as the literal `/tmp/ped-fresh-<run>`, bypassing the repository's scratch-placement owner `imas_ambix/gs/artifact_resolution.py:149` (`staging_cache_root()`), whose docstring and test (`tests/gs/test_artifact_resolution.py:249` "A SLURM node's own scratch is reached through `TMPDIR`, not `/tmp`") make `TMPDIR` the node-local root with `/tmp` only the fallback; the dispatch contract for this repo ('a temporary tree ... goes under `$TMPDIR`, never a bare `/tmp` path, so it dies with the run's scratch') states the same rule

findings.reason: the section must either fold the proof into the existing census module (`tests/test_declared_dependencies.py`, which already owns the optional definition and ships a callable entry point) so no new surface is added, or state in its own text what the added surface replaces.
findings.text: §4 stands up a fresh-environment proof (build the environment, walk and import every module, run the console script, collect the suite, run ruff) as a new entry point, adding to a week whose supplied budget is public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0, yet the section names nothing it retires or merges and does not say why nothing can be

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the census hides import walking, distribution mapping, classification, transitive closure, rendering and the assertion behind the one `build_census()` entry point, and §4/§5 add no competing module.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4 hardcodes node-local scratch as a bare `/tmp` path, forking the repository's scratch-placement owner instead of extending it.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §4 introduces a fresh-environment proof entry point (a new module plus its callable/console surface) without naming anything it retires or merges, or stating why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites `tests/test_declared_dependencies.py` for the optional definition, but `build_census()` is environment-dependent and does not deliver the shared "classed optional" set inside the fresh environment.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §4 adds a proof over the existing census entry point rather than a layer that forwards to it, and §5 adds pytest marks to existing tests; neither introduces a thin parallel mechanism needing justification.
